name: JS-modules
origin: Extracted from Apple Press, https://github.com/lfcfoundry/apple-press (play: https://lfcfoundry.github.io/apple-press/), and Fancy, the Banana, https://github.com/lfcfoundry/fancy-banana (play: https://lfcfoundry.github.io/fancy-banana/)

modules.summary: Velvet stage curtains that slide shut over a page, then fly open.
Safe localStorage saves, backup slot, checksummed copy-paste save codes with a size limit on what a paste may unpack to.
Hold-to-repeat for buttons that survives Android Chrome pointercancel.
Detects privacy modes that round timers (including Firefox's 16.67 ms clock), scramble canvas read-back or block storage, and says what it found in plain words.
Steps visual effects down when the device cannot keep up; never back up behind the player.
A big element scrolls away and a copy flies to its sticky mini version (and back).
Die-cut sticker lettering in plain CSS text-shadow rings, no images.
Tested maths for idle/clicker games: costs, buy-many and buy-max, milestones, away income, boost queue, number format.

Frame pacing for canvas games: even-dt smooths the frame time, quality-governor steps effects down and back up, job-pump spreads heavy jobs across frames, frame-meter shows frames a second, hitches and tap delay in plain words.
Tiny software 3D rasterizer that bakes shaded sprites to canvases once at load, or one frame per tick; also makes silhouette masks and packs sprite sheets.
Gamepad API to DOM focus: move through buttons, menus, sliders and drop-downs with a controller, no game code.
Keeps one open copy of a page in charge (Web Locks), so two tabs do not overwrite each other's saved data, and tells the game when the other copy closes.
Keeps the screen awake only while a game wants it: released on pause, hidden tab and idle, asked again when allowed, no retry storms.
Makes the phone back swipe or back button close the top panel instead of leaving the page (CloseWatcher, with an opt-in history fallback for browsers without it).
Small readable LZMA1 decoder (ES5), tested against Python's lzma. Browsers can only unpack gzip and deflate natively.

A PPMd (7-Zip PPMd7) decoder in one ES5 function, about 6.6 KB packed. It unpacks web-page data about 10% smaller than LZMA, but about 4 times slower. PPMd is by Dmitry Shkarin; the public-domain code it follows is Igor Pavlov's, from 7-Zip.
A written style guide plus demo for the soft, glossy cartoon 3D look done in plain CSS and SVG.
Writes animated GIFs from canvas pictures with one shared palette, storing only the pixels that changed (about 6.8 times smaller than gifenc on a mostly still animation).
Opens .zip and Excel .xlsx files safely: limits counted on what really unpacks, so a zip bomb stops at the limit with a plain-words note.
Lays out a flow chart (Sankey) from a plain list of links, with about half the weighted crossings of d3-sankey on the charts measured, backward links drawn instead of crashing, and an SVG drawer.
Simulates random walkers on a network with seeded, repeatable runs, 16 random-number distributions, 95% ranges and the exact odds to check against (about 1.75 million walkers a second).
Keeps a short note, only on the device, of the errors, slow taps and long frames a page had; copyable as plain text, nothing is sent anywhere.
A hold-then-drag task a young child will not finish, in front of the buttons and links a grown-up should press (a speed bump, not security).
A first-time tour: one dimmed layer, a bright window over the current part, Skip and Back, remembers who saw it and gives a finishing gift once.

tools.summary: Font subsetting, safe inline-SVG tightening and a Zopfli self-extracting packer for one-file games.
Packs one HTML file into a smaller self-unpacking file with LZMA and a hash check (Python 3 standard library).

Packs one HTML file into a self-unpacking file with PPMd, the 7-Zip text compressor (PPMd by Dmitry Shkarin; public-domain code by Igor Pavlov, 7-Zip). Pure Python; pays off above about 60 KB of compressed data.

Seeded, reproducible random-input fuzzer engine with weighted operations, invariants, liveness checks and failure shrinking; Playwright and Puppeteer runners with real input and CPU throttling; stock-Firefox recipe; test-hook stripper.
Test-build counter for canvas 2D games: calls per frame, save/restore leaks, overhanging drawImage sources, draws below half size, style-write repeats, painted area.
Page that tells you in plain words whether copies of a page saved in different folders share their saved data, see each other's writes and locks; one button, copyable report.
Runs a Playwright-for-Python test in stock Firefox (through Selenium and geckodriver) without rewriting it; says plainly which calls it supports and stops with a clear message on the rest.

Drives WebKitGTK or GNOME Web from Node with no dependencies, using the call names of Playwright and Puppeteer (goto, evaluate, waitForFunction, mouse, keyboard, screenshot, console errors), so a test written for them can also run in WebKit.
Puts a prefix in front of every localStorage key on a test page, so a speed test or random-play run never touches the real saved game.
One-button speed test run on the device: compares your page with parts switched off, keeps the scene in view and uncovered, and says the answer in plain sentences with a copyable table.

related.note: Story packages live with the editor they are generated from.

packages.summary: Create, clean, search, import and export interactive stories as JSON, with a JSON Schema. Twine import lives in twine-import.
Reads Twine stories (Twine 2 HTML, Twee 3, Twine 1) and turns SugarCube and Harlowe code into rules, with a plain-words report.
Turns an indented outline into pages and choices, or into a whole branching story.
Says in plain words what one edit did to a story, such as "Add page “The Cellar”".
Exact checker for branching stories with items, numbers and dice: dead ends and endings no player can reach.
Build one offline HTML game from a story, or play a story from code or a terminal.
Layered, arc and matrix drawings of a story graph (SVG) and seeded simulated players.
Wrap a finished HTML page into a smaller page that unzips itself, with a pure-JS inflater fallback.
Tiered test runner and a Playwright-style API over WebDriver BiDi for stock Firefox; seeded random-story generator.
A guide and a small helper for keeping two implementations of one rule set from drifting apart: seeded random inputs, a side-by-side comparison, a field table and a time limit.
A written process and templates for a person and an AI assistant building software together.
